## Introduction

The `TFGproject` package provides an easy-to-use implementation of the Marascuilo procedure. This test is typically used after a significant Chi-square test to determine exactly which groups differ from each other when comparing multiple proportions.

## Setup

First, load the package and `ggplot2` into your environment:

```{r setup}
library(TFGproject)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Example Data

Let's create a sample dataset representing a survey about a specific opinion across three different cities:

```{r data}
df_ejemplo <- data.frame(
  City = c(rep("Cordoba", 150), rep("Villa Maria", 75), rep("Rio IV", 75)),
  Opinion = c(
    rep("Agree", 115), rep("Disagree", 35),
    rep("Agree", 53), rep("Disagree", 22),
    rep("Agree", 40), rep("Disagree", 35)
  )
)
```

## Running the Test

We use the `marascuilo_test()` function. We need to specify the dataset, the grouping column, the response column, and the specific value that represents a "success" (in this case, "Agree").

```{r test}
resultados <- marascuilo_test(
  df = df_ejemplo, 
  col_grupo = "City", 
  col_respuesta = "Opinion", 
  valor_exito = "Agree"
)
```

## Results and Visualization

Because the package uses a custom S3 class architecture, you can simply print the object to see the results and which comparisons are statistically significant:

```{r print}
resultados
```

To visually interpret these results, use the `autoplot()` function. It will automatically generate a `ggplot2` chart comparing the absolute differences against the critical ranges for each pair:

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
ggplot2::autoplot(resultados)
```

## Sample Data and Shiny Application

The package includes a built-in CSV sample dataset. You can access its path and load it using `system.file()`:

```{r csv_example}
ruta_csv <- system.file("extdata", "datos_ejemplo.csv", package = "TFGproject")
datos_csv <- read.csv(ruta_csv)
head(datos_csv)
```

To launch the interactive Shiny web application included in the package, run the following command in your R console:

```r
shiny::runApp(system.file("app", package = "TFGproject"))
```
